playbook:
When I must pledge, if I can only afford scout I pledge scout.

I always account that the pledge cost is deducted immediately from my fuel; I plan endgame fuel value (unused fuel = points) when choosing costly pledges.

I will not pledge raid as a bluff. I will only pledge raid if I intend to perform that raid on the act stage that same round.

Before pledging raid I require that my current fuel ≥ 2 (the pledge cost) and that I am committed to spending it now; I will only pledge raid if I will actually submit act: raid that round.

When I have ≥2 fuel and opponents have been reliably scouting, I will schedule a timed raid (pledge + act) in a round where that raid meaningfully swings the score (±3 points matters), targeting the clockwise player who is scouting without escort.

When I am leading and an opponent to my left is likely to raid clockwise into me, I will pledge escort to block theft and protect my score.

When tied or slightly behind in late rounds and a clockwise raid could swing the game, I will pledge raid only if I am certain I will execute it that round and I have the fuel to pay the immediate cost; otherwise I choose scout or escort as appropriate.

When opponents show mixed signals (some scouts, some escorts), I prefer escort if I’m vulnerable to incoming raids, or scout if I want guaranteed points and I’m not the raid target.

When deciding between scout and escort, prefer scout when I want guaranteed points and am not the likely raid target; prefer escort when I expect incoming theft or want to deny a coordinated raid.

When submitting my act, I always match my pledge. I will not plan to switch at act stage; the pledge is my committed action for that round.

When everyone pledged scout, I will only switch to raid if I pledged raid that round; otherwise I take scout (or escort if I pledged escort). I will not assume I can convert to a raid on the act stage without having pledged it.

When fuel is low (0–1), avoid pledging anything but scout; prioritize conserving fuel for end-of-game fuel-to-points conversion.

When deciding whether to raid, raid only if the clockwise target is scoring scouts without escort and the ±3 point swing materially helps my standing, factoring opponents’ likely next-round responses and my remaining fuel value.

If I expect a coordinated two-player raid on one target, use escort to protect that target if it’s me; if I can’t protect myself, prefer to scout to bank points or raid elsewhere only if I can execute.

Avoid sequences that leave me with too little fuel to benefit from endgame fuel points unless the immediate scoring swing is worth it; preserve enough fuel late to convert unused fuel to points when that matters.

Keep commitments transparent: my pledges should reflect my intended acts so opponents can be predicted and I avoid miscoordination that wastes fuel.

Require a simple fuel rule for pledging risky actions: I will not pledge raid unless I have ≥2 fuel now and full intention to act raid; I will not pledge escort unless I have ≥2 fuel now and need the protection or want to deny a raid.

Read opponent patterns: if two opponents repeatedly scout, one well-timed, executed raid can swing a tied late game — plan that only when I can and will execute it.

If leading near the end with low fuel, prioritize escort (if vulnerable) or scout to collect guaranteed points and preserve final fuel value rather than risky raids.

If I pledge raid and then, due to some error or realization, I cannot execute it, treat that as an avoidable mistake to be eliminated—do not repeat conflicting pledge/act behavior.
